title: The Man Counting Donkeys

full_text:
Nasruddin bought nine donkeys at the market and rode one of them toward home. Along the road, he counted the animals: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight! Alas! A donkey is missing!"

He leaped down from his saddle in panic, searched behind the bushes, and counted again: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine! Ah, it has returned!"

He mounted his donkey again and rode on. After a mile, he counted once more: "Eight again! A demon is stealing my donkeys!"

His wife met him at the gate: "Husband, what is the matter?"

"I bought nine donkeys, but whenever I ride, there are only eight; and whenever I walk, there are nine!"

His wife shook her head: "I see ten donkeys! Nine on four legs, and one on two legs sitting on top of the first!"
moral: People often count all external things while forgetting the vehicle that carries them.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Man Counting Donkeys"?
options: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
